From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Daughter of Dryops or of Eurytus, mother of Amphissus

For other uses, see [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope "Dryope").

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/73/Dr%C3%ADope_transformada_em_l%C3%B3tus.jpg/250px-Dr%C3%ADope_transformada_em_l%C3%B3tus.jpg)](/wiki/File:Dr%C3%ADope_transformada_em_l%C3%B3tus.jpg)

Dríope transformed into a [lotus tree](/wiki/Nelumbo "Nelumbo") illustration extracted out of [Ovid](/wiki/Ovid "Ovid")'s [Metamorphoses](/wiki/Metamorphoses "Metamorphoses")

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology"), **Dryope** ([/ˈdraɪ.əpiː/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Δρυόπη) is the daughter of [Dryops, king of Oeta](/wiki/Dryops_(Oeta) "Dryops (Oeta)") ("oak-man")[[1]](#cite_note-:0-1) or of [Eurytus](/wiki/Eurytus,_king_of_Oechalia "Eurytus, king of Oechalia") (and hence half-sister to [Iole](/wiki/Iole "Iole")).[[2]](#cite_note-:1-2) Dryope mothered [Amphissus](/wiki/Amphissus "Amphissus") by [Apollo](/wiki/Apollo "Apollo").[[1]](#cite_note-:0-1)

Mythology
---------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Mythology")]

There is a story of her [metamorphosis](/wiki/Shapeshifting "Shapeshifting") into a [black poplar](/wiki/Black_poplar "Black poplar"), and a story of her changing into a lotus tree.

### Antoninus Liberalis' account

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Antoninus Liberalis' account")]

According to the first, Apollo seduced her by a trick. While Dryope tended the flocks of her father on Mount Oeta, she became the playmate of the [hamadryads](/wiki/Hamadryad "Hamadryad") of the woods on [Mount Oeta](/wiki/Mount_Oeta "Mount Oeta"). The nymphs taught her to sing hymns to the gods and to dance. On one occasion, Dryope was seen by Apollo. In order to win her favours the god turned himself into a [tortoise](/wiki/Tortoise "Tortoise"), of which the girls made a pet. The nymphs played with the animal and when Dryope had the tortoise on her lap, Apollo turned into a snake. The nymphs then got scared and abandoned her, and Apollo raped her. Eventually she gave birth to her son Amphissus. Soon afterwards Dryope married [Andraemon](/wiki/Andraemon "Andraemon"), son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus"). Amphissus eventually built a temple to his father Apollo in the city of Oeta, which he founded. Here the nymphs came to converse with Dryope, who had become a priestess of the temple. Fond of her, they took her with them and placed a poplar tree in her place. They then turned her into a nymph. Two [women](/wiki/Oechalides "Oechalides") of the town told the people that the nymphs had taken Dryope, so the nymphs turned them into fir trees.[[3]](#cite_note-3)

### Ovid's account

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Ovid's account")]

In [Ovid](/wiki/Ovid "Ovid")'s version of the story,[[2]](#cite_note-:1-2) Dryope was wandering by a lake, suckling her baby Amphissus, when she saw the bright red flowers of the lotus, formerly the nymph [Lotis](/wiki/Lotis_(mythology) "Lotis (mythology)") who, when fleeing from [Priapus](/wiki/Priapus "Priapus"), had been changed into a tree. Dryope wanted to give the blossoms to her baby to play with, but when she picked one the tree started to tremble and bleed. She tried to run away, but the blood of the tree had touched her skin and she found her feet rooted to the spot. She slowly began to turn into a lotus tree, the bark spreading up her legs from the earth, but just before the woody stiffness finally reached her throat and as her arms began sprouting twigs her husband Andraemon heard her cries and came to her. She had just enough time to warn her husband to take care of their child and make sure that he did not pick flowers. She also told him to find Amphissus a nurse and to tell him to call her his mother.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Greek mythological figures

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology"), **Oxylus** ([/ˈɒksɪləs/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ὄξυλος, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Óxulos*) may refer to:

* Oxylus, *[daimon](/wiki/Daimon "Daimon")* of the mountain [beech](/wiki/Beech "Beech") forests, son of [Orius](/wiki/Oreius_(mythology) "Oreius (mythology)") ([mountain-god](/wiki/Ourea "Ourea") of [Othrys](/wiki/Mount_Othrys "Mount Othrys") or the [Pindus](/wiki/Pindus "Pindus")), who is noted in the [Deipnosophistae](/wiki/Deipnosophistae "Deipnosophistae") for fathering the [Hamadryads](/wiki/Hamadryad "Hamadryad") with his own sister [Hamadryas](/wiki/Hamadryas_(mythology) "Hamadryas (mythology)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Oxylus, son for [Ares](/wiki/Ares "Ares") and [Protogeneia](/wiki/Protogeneia "Protogeneia"), daughter of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon").[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus_(son_of_Haemon) "Oxylus (son of Haemon)"), king of [Elis](/wiki/Ancient_Elis "Ancient Elis"); from [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"), son of [Haemon](/wiki/Haemon_(mythology) "Haemon (mythology)") (himself son of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)")) or of [Andraemon](/wiki/Andraemon "Andraemon").[[3]](#cite_note-3)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Daughter of Dryops or of Eurytus, mother of Amphissus

For other uses, see [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope "Dryope").

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/73/Dr%C3%ADope_transformada_em_l%C3%B3tus.jpg/250px-Dr%C3%ADope_transformada_em_l%C3%B3tus.jpg)](/wiki/File:Dr%C3%ADope_transformada_em_l%C3%B3tus.jpg)

Dríope transformed into a [lotus tree](/wiki/Nelumbo "Nelumbo") illustration extracted out of [Ovid](/wiki/Ovid "Ovid")'s [Metamorphoses](/wiki/Metamorphoses "Metamorphoses")

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology"), **Dryope** ([/ˈdraɪ.əpiː/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Δρυόπη) is the daughter of [Dryops, king of Oeta](/wiki/Dryops_(Oeta) "Dryops (Oeta)") ("oak-man")[[1]](#cite_note-:0-1) or of [Eurytus](/wiki/Eurytus,_king_of_Oechalia "Eurytus, king of Oechalia") (and hence half-sister to [Iole](/wiki/Iole "Iole")).[[2]](#cite_note-:1-2) Dryope mothered [Amphissus](/wiki/Amphissus "Amphissus") by [Apollo](/wiki/Apollo "Apollo").[[1]](#cite_note-:0-1)

Mythology
---------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Mythology")]

There is a story of her [metamorphosis](/wiki/Shapeshifting "Shapeshifting") into a [black poplar](/wiki/Black_poplar "Black poplar"), and a story of her changing into a lotus tree.

### Antoninus Liberalis' account

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Antoninus Liberalis' account")]

According to the first, Apollo seduced her by a trick. While Dryope tended the flocks of her father on Mount Oeta, she became the playmate of the [hamadryads](/wiki/Hamadryad "Hamadryad") of the woods on [Mount Oeta](/wiki/Mount_Oeta "Mount Oeta"). The nymphs taught her to sing hymns to the gods and to dance. On one occasion, Dryope was seen by Apollo. In order to win her favours the god turned himself into a [tortoise](/wiki/Tortoise "Tortoise"), of which the girls made a pet. The nymphs played with the animal and when Dryope had the tortoise on her lap, Apollo turned into a snake. The nymphs then got scared and abandoned her, and Apollo raped her. Eventually she gave birth to her son Amphissus. Soon afterwards Dryope married [Andraemon](/wiki/Andraemon "Andraemon"), son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus"). Amphissus eventually built a temple to his father Apollo in the city of Oeta, which he founded. Here the nymphs came to converse with Dryope, who had become a priestess of the temple. Fond of her, they took her with them and placed a poplar tree in her place. They then turned her into a nymph. Two [women](/wiki/Oechalides "Oechalides") of the town told the people that the nymphs had taken Dryope, so the nymphs turned them into fir trees.[[3]](#cite_note-3)

### Ovid's account

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Ovid's account")]

In [Ovid](/wiki/Ovid "Ovid")'s version of the story,[[2]](#cite_note-:1-2) Dryope was wandering by a lake, suckling her baby Amphissus, when she saw the bright red flowers of the lotus, formerly the nymph [Lotis](/wiki/Lotis_(mythology) "Lotis (mythology)") who, when fleeing from [Priapus](/wiki/Priapus "Priapus"), had been changed into a tree. Dryope wanted to give the blossoms to her baby to play with, but when she picked one the tree started to tremble and bleed. She tried to run away, but the blood of the tree had touched her skin and she found her feet rooted to the spot. She slowly began to turn into a lotus tree, the bark spreading up her legs from the earth, but just before the woody stiffness finally reached her throat and as her arms began sprouting twigs her husband Andraemon heard her cries and came to her. She had just enough time to warn her husband to take care of their child and make sure that he did not pick flowers. She also told him to find Amphissus a nurse and to tell him to call her his mother.

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology"), **Oxylus** ([/ˈɒksɪləs/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ὄξυλος, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Óxulos*) may refer to:

* Oxylus, *[daimon](/wiki/Daimon "Daimon")* of the mountain [beech](/wiki/Beech "Beech") forests, son of [Orius](/wiki/Oreius_(mythology) "Oreius (mythology)") ([mountain-god](/wiki/Ourea "Ourea") of [Othrys](/wiki/Mount_Othrys "Mount Othrys") or the [Pindus](/wiki/Pindus "Pindus")), who is noted in the [Deipnosophistae](/wiki/Deipnosophistae "Deipnosophistae") for fathering the [Hamadryads](/wiki/Hamadryad "Hamadryad") with his own sister [Hamadryas](/wiki/Hamadryas_(mythology) "Hamadryas (mythology)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Oxylus, son for [Ares](/wiki/Ares "Ares") and [Protogeneia](/wiki/Protogeneia "Protogeneia"), daughter of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon").[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus_(son_of_Haemon) "Oxylus (son of Haemon)"), king of [Elis](/wiki/Ancient_Elis "Ancient Elis"); from [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"), son of [Haemon](/wiki/Haemon_(mythology) "Haemon (mythology)") (himself son of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)")) or of [Andraemon](/wiki/Andraemon "Andraemon").[[3]](#cite_note-3)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

In [Greek mythology](/wiki/Greek_mythology "Greek mythology") the name **Andraemon** ([/ænˈdriːmən/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀνδραίμων, [romanized](/wiki/Romanization_of_Ancient_Greek "Romanization of Ancient Greek"): *Andraímon*) may refer to:

* Andraemon, son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus "Oxylus") and husband of [Dryope](/wiki/Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops) "Dryope (daughter of Dryops)").[[1]](#cite_note-1)
* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)
* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia") king and husband of [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)") of [Calydon](/wiki/Calydon "Calydon"). By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus "Oeneus")' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia "Aetolia"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa "Amfissa").[[3]](#cite_note-3)
* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) "Leonteus (mythology)"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome "Amphinome"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias "Pelias").[[4]](#cite_note-4)
* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope "Suitors of Penelope") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope "Penelope") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium "Dulichium") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus "Odysseus") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus "Eumaeus"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) "Philoetius (Odyssey)"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus "Telemachus").[[6]](#cite_note-6)
* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus "Codrus"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor "Asia Minor") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria "Caria") out of the city of Lebedus. His tomb was shown near [Colophon](/wiki/Colophon_(city) "Colophon (city)").[[7]](#cite_note-7) [Mimnermus](/wiki/Mimnermus "Mimnermus") related that Andraemon was a native of [Pylos](/wiki/Pylos "Pylos") and founder of Colophon.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Similarly **Andraemonides** was a [patronymic](/wiki/Patronymic "Patronymic"), frequently used to refer to [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) "Thoas (king of Aetoila)"), son of Andraemon and [Gorge](/wiki/Gorge_(mythology) "Gorge (mythology)").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

(daughter of Dryops)\").[[1]](#cite_note-1)\\n* Andraemon, possible father of another Oxylus.[[2]](#cite_note-2)\\n* Andraemon, an [Aetolian](/wiki/Aetolia \"Aetolia\") king and husband of By the latter, he became the father of [Thoas](/wiki/Thoas_(king_of_Aetoila) \"Thoas (king of Aetoila)\"). Andraemon succeeded his father-in-law [Oeneus](/wiki/Oeneus \"Oeneus\")\\' power over [Aetolia](/wiki/Aetolia \"Aetolia\"). He and his wife were buried in one tomb which was shown in the city of [Amphissa](/wiki/Amfissa \"Amfissa\").[[3]](#cite_note-3)\\n* Andraemon, brother of [Leonteus](/wiki/Leonteus_(mythology) \"Leonteus (mythology)\"). He married [Amphinome](/wiki/Amphinome \"Amphinome\"), a daughter of [Pelias](/wiki/Pelias \"Pelias\").[[4]](#cite_note-4)\\n* Andraemon, one of the [Suitors](/wiki/Suitors_of_Penelope \"Suitors of Penelope\") of [Penelope](/wiki/Penelope \"Penelope\") who came from [Dulichium](/wiki/Dulichium \"Dulichium\") along with other 56 wooers.[[5]](#cite_note-5) He, with the other suitors, was slain by [Odysseus](/wiki/Odysseus \"Odysseus\") with the aid of [Eumaeus](/wiki/Eumaeus \"Eumaeus\"), [Philoetius](/wiki/Philoetius_(Odyssey) \"Philoetius (Odyssey)\"), and [Telemachus](/wiki/Telemachus \"Telemachus\").[[6]](#cite_note-6)\\n* Andraemon, a son of King [Codrus](/wiki/Codrus \"Codrus\"). He participated in the colonization of [Asia Minor](/wiki/Asia_Minor \"Asia Minor\") and drove the [Carians](/wiki/Caria \"Caria\") out of the city of Lebedus. Mythology\")]\\n\\nThere is a story of her [metamorphosis](/wiki/Shapeshifting \"Shapeshifting\") into a [black poplar](/wiki/Black_poplar \"Black poplar\"), and a story of her changing into a lotus tree.\\n\\n### Antoninus Liberalis\\' account\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops)&action=edit&section=2 \"Edit section: Antoninus Liberalis\\' account\")]\\n\\nAccording to the first, Apollo seduced her by a trick. While Dryope tended the flocks of her father on Mount Oeta, she became the playmate of the [hamadryads](/wiki/Hamadryad \"Hamadryad\") of the woods on [Mount Oeta](/wiki/Mount_Oeta \"Mount Oeta\"). The nymphs taught her to sing hymns to the gods and to dance. On one occasion, Dryope was seen by Apollo. In order to win her favours the god turned himself into a [tortoise](/wiki/Tortoise \"Tortoise\"), of which the girls made a pet. The nymphs played with the animal and when Dryope had the tortoise on her lap, Apollo turned into a snake. The nymphs then got scared and abandoned her, and Apollo raped her. Eventually she gave birth to her son Amphissus. Soon afterwards Dryope married [Andraemon](/wiki/Andraemon \"Andraemon\"), son of [Oxylus](/wiki/Oxylus \"Oxylus\"). Amphissus eventually built a temple to his father Apollo in the city of Oeta, which he founded. Here the nymphs came to converse with Dryope, who had become a priestess of the temple. Fond of her, they took her with them and placed a poplar tree in her place. They then turned her into a nymph. Two [women](/wiki/Oechalides \"Oechalides\") of the town told the people that the nymphs had taken Dryope, so the nymphs turned them into fir trees.[[3]](#cite_note-3)\\n\\n### Ovid\\'s account\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops)&action=edit&section=3 \"Edit section: Ovid\\'s account\")]\\n\\nIn [Ovid](/wiki/Ovid \"Ovid\")\\'s version of the story,[[2]](#cite_note-:1-2) Dryope was wandering by a lake, suckling her baby Amphissus, when she saw the bright red flowers of the lotus, formerly the nymph [Lotis](/wiki/Lotis_(mythology) \"Lotis (mythology)\") who, when fleeing from [Priapus](/wiki/Priapus \"Priapus\"), had been changed into a tree. Dryope wanted to give the blossoms to her baby to play with, but when she picked one the tree started to tremble and bleed. She tried to run away, but the blood of the tree had touched her skin and she found her feet rooted to the spot. She slowly began to turn into a lotus tree, the bark spreading up her legs from the earth, but just before the woody stiffness finally reached her throat and as her arms began sprouting twigs her husband Andraemon heard her cries and came to her. She had just enough time to warn her husband to take care of their child and make sure that he did not pick flowers. She also told him to find Amphissus a nurse and to tell him to call her his mother.\\n\\nNotes\\n-----\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops)&action=edit&section=4 \"Edit section: Notes\")]\\n\\n1. ^ [***a***](#cite_ref-:0_1-0) [***b***](#cite_ref-:0_1-1) [Antoninus Liberalis](/wiki/Antoninus_Liberalis \"Antoninus Liberalis\"), [32](https://topostext.org/work/216#32); [Stephanus Byzantinus](/wiki/Stephanus_Byzantinus \"Stephanus Byzantinus\"), s.v. *Dryope*.\\n2. ^ [***a***](#cite_ref-:1_2-0) [***b***](#cite_ref-:1_2-1) Ovid, *[Metamorphoses](/wiki/Metamorphoses \"Metamorphoses\")* 9.325ff.\\n3. **[^](#cite_ref-3)** Antoninus Liberalis, [32](https://topostext.org/work/216#32)\\n\\nReferences\\n----------\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Dryope_(daughter_of_Dryops)&action=edit&section=5 \"Edit section: References\")]\\n\\n* [Antoninus Liberalis](/wiki/Antoninus_Liberalis \"Antoninus Liberalis\"), *The Metamorphoses of Antoninus Liberalis: A Translation with a Commentary*, edited and translated by Francis Celoria, Routledge, 1992.
